chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one who is afflicted with conjunctivitis during the month of Ramadan: can he sprinkle his eyes during the day while he is fasting? He said: He sprinkles it when he breaks the fast, and he does not sprinkle it while he is fasting.

key_terms.يَذُرُّ: To sprinkle or drop (liquid into the eye)

ai.seo_question: Does putting eye drops break the fast in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the specific condition of 'ramad' (conjunctivitis) is addressed to clarify whether applying medicinal drops or kohl breaks the fast. The Imam distinguishes between the general principle that the eyes are not a primary passage for nourishment and the specific practical ruling that one should ideally apply the drops after breaking the fast to avoid any doubt, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on caution (ihtiyat) in matters of worship while maintaining the integrity of the fast.
